content:
Maria: Heads up — compliance asked for a compact 'actor evidence' download flow for change events. Want to discuss quota + UI constraints before we scope export shape. TL;DR: keep payload small (no full diff), include actor id, role, timestamp, justification, and a short anchor to full snapshot.
Dan: ok, what's the expected frequency? ad-hoc or scheduled pulls?
Maria: Mostly ad-hoc during audits. A tenant might request a few dozen small exports on review days.
Aliya: We already have export quotas per-tenant/day. Need to think about legal-hold exemptions and who can bypass.
Sam: For compact payloads NDJSON streaming + presigned S3 link seems simplest. But rate limits will still be hit if many users request concurrently.
Jeff: Also PII/redaction modes — exports should support redaction toggles. That affects both payload shape and approval.
Olivia: UX idea: console shows two options: "Compact (actor evidence)" vs "Full snapshot" and shows estimated size + required approvals.
Maria: Also want each record to include a proof anchor (HMAC signature) so downstream auditors can verify integrity without needing the whole snapshot.
Dan: HMAC adds ~88 chars per event (base64 sig). That will change our size estimates and quota math.
Aliya: Can we treat the proof as metadata that doesn't count against user download quotas? Concern: workaround for egress limits.
Sam: From infra side, bandwidth still counts. If we exempt it logically, billing and SLOs get complicated. Better to surface cost and require approval.
Maria: Proposal: default compact export includes: hashed_actor_id, role, timestamp, short_summary (<=280 chars), justification, proof_anchor (short sig). Full snapshot remains opt-in with stricter permission + justification required.
Jeff: Permission model: snapshot exports need an elevated scope and an approval workflow in console. We should log who approved and attach to export.
Olivia: I'll mock a one-click request flow: user picks export type, sees cost estimate, picks redaction toggle, enters justification; snapshot requests show approver list.
deploy-bot: deployment to staging succeeded for feature/compact-export-ux (build #7421) :rocket:
Maria: Can eng-sre review rate-limit behaviour before we prod this? Need to avoid noisy billing surprises.
Sam: Will add a canary policy: 10 rps per tenant, burst 50, default quota 1 GiB/day for exports. We can tune after telemetry.
Aliya: Legal-hold mode: add a tag that bypasses soft quotas but triggers manual approval and billing alert to Sales/Finance.
Jeff: Telemetry needs: per-export token usage, bytes/event, redaction percentage, number of snapshot vs compact exports. We should emit these as metrics and a daily export report.
Dan: API shape suggestion: POST /audit/exports {"type":"compact|snapshot", "redaction":true|false, "date_range":{start,end}, "justification":string} -> returns {"status":"queued","presigned_url":string} or a streaming endpoint. Thoughts?
Maria: That shape looks good. Make "justification" required for snapshot exports and optional for compact; record required for audit trail.
Olivia: I'll prepare a quick console mock and cost calc.
Jeff: I can draft permission docs and a snippet for IAM mapping.
Sam: Adding PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/1234 with initial config.
Maria: Thanks — I'll schedule a sync Thurs 11am to lock API shape and quotas. Calendar invite incoming.
Jeff: @Maria ping me if you want the permission doc before the sync.
Olivia: I'll include the mock + accessibility notes in the invite.
Maria: Closing notes: keep compact payload intentionally small, attach verifiable proof anchors, require justification for snapshots, and implement a canary quota before full rollout.
